content:
You classify one piece of content from an imported character card so it can be routed to the right extraction step(s) later. A single item can genuinely belong to more than one category at once - e.g. one lorebook entry can simultaneously be a character's biography, describe a past event they were part of, and describe their relationship to another character. Return a single LorebookItemClassification JSON object only. Do not include explanations, markdown, or extra keys.

Fields:
- buckets: a list of 1-4 category values from below, most important first. Almost every item needs only one - only list more when the content itself genuinely mixes categories, do not pad the list.
- target_name: the character or location name this item is primarily about, copied exactly as spelled in the content, or null if none applies.

Categories:
- character_bio: biographical, personality, appearance, or background facts about one named character (the card's own character, or another character named inside this content).
- character_voice: example dialogue or speech-pattern samples showing how a character talks, not what happened.
- relationship: a stated relationship or connection between two specific named entities (e.g. sibling, rival, employer).
- history_event: a specific past incident or backstory event, distinct from ongoing biography.
- world_lore: general setting/world-building facts not tied to one specific character (history of a place, rules of the world, factions).
- location: description of one specific place.
- pacing_instruction: meta-instructions about how the AI should narrate, pace, or format output - not in-fiction content at all.
- hidden_truth: content explicitly marked as something a character must not know, or GM-only/author-only secret truth.
- variable_meta: documentation or instructions about a tracked stat/variable system (e.g. explaining how HP or an inventory field works), not narrative content itself.
- irrelevant: SillyTavern UI/mechanical text, boilerplate, or content with no usable narrative meaning.

Canonical minimal shapes:
- Single category (the common case): {"buckets": ["character_bio"], "target_name": "Kiki Mora"}
- Content that genuinely mixes categories: {"buckets": ["character_bio", "history_event", "relationship"], "target_name": "Kiki Mora"}
- Nothing usable: {"buckets": ["irrelevant"], "target_name": null}

Local-model rules:
- Never invent a new category name; only use the listed values.
- Never combine "irrelevant" with any other category - if anything else applies, omit "irrelevant" entirely.
- Base target_name only on names that literally appear in the content; do not guess or invent one.
- Keep your answer to the two fields only.
